source: sars-guide:PAYE-GEN-01-G21 Rev 1 p. 11-12 (employer medical contribution is a taxable fringe benefit, deemed paid by the employee: code 3810 added to 4005; medical scheme fees tax credit R376 / R376 / R254)
sourceRef: https://www.sars.gov.za/wp-content/uploads/Ops/Guides/PAYE-GEN-01-G21-Guide-for-Employers-iro-Employees-Tax-for-2027-External-Guide.pdf ; SARS e@syFile Employer Reconciliation BRS (SARS_PAYE_BRS V25.3.0, Jun-26) codes 3810 p. 94, 4474 p. 103
notes: R25 000 salary; the employer pays R3 000 a month to a medical scheme for the employee and one dependant. G21 p. 12: that contribution is a taxable fringe benefit, deemed paid by the employee, so code 3810 (R3 000) is remuneration and the same value counts as deemed contributions (4005) for the medical scheme fees tax credit: R376 + R376 = R752 a month (G21 p. 11, 2027). Taxable 28 000; x12 = 336 000; tax = 44 118 + 26% x (336 000 - 245 100) = 67 752; less 17 820 = 49 932; /12 = 4 161.00; less R752 = 3409.00. The Seventh Schedule para 12A / s6A-6B wording is not fetched (named limit); the G21 p. 11-12 text is the source. The 3810 earning is entered as taxable cash here because the oracle component type cannot carry a non-cash benefit; employer UIF/SDL on it are not asserted.
